stories.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had continued attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite President Donald Trump's surprise announcement that Kyiv and Moscow had agreed to an energy ceasefire. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had not been informed of the arrangement but would support a real truce, and called on Washington to ensure Russia complied. Russian strikes hit Ukrainian power plants on Sunday, causing outages, while Moscow had not confirmed an accord. European leaders said they had seen no evidence that a ceasefire was operating, and the EU announced nearly 1,600 additional sanctions targeting Russia's military-industrial complex.
stories.headline: Ukraine says Russia violated Trump's announced energy ceasefire

stories.body: Saudi Arabia extended the suspension of flights at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport after another Houthi missile attack caused damage and killed one person, following a strike the previous day that killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Saudi authorities said the airport would remain closed while its safety was verified and said additional missile and drone threats had been detected. The Iran-backed Houthis said the attacks were retaliation for Saudi military action in Yemen, where fighting has intensified after a fragile informal ceasefire began to unravel in July.
stories.headline: Saudi Arabia extends Riyadh airport closure after further Houthi attacks

stories.body: Iran urged Saudi Arabia to seek a political settlement with Yemen's Houthi movement after deadly attacks on Saudi airports, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi telling his Saudi counterpart that a military approach would worsen the crisis. Tehran said it was ready to help start dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, while its foreign ministry said it did not want hostilities to continue between two Muslim countries. The offer followed a second Houthi attack on Riyadh airport and renewed questions over the extent of Iranian coordination with the group.
stories.headline: Iran offers to facilitate talks as Saudi-Houthi conflict escalates

stories.body: The European Union will limit annual imports of hybrid electric vehicles from China to 350,000 under a four-year agreement reached in Beijing, the European Commission said. The quota, due to take effect in December under World Trade Organization safeguard rules, is expected to cut China's EU market share roughly in half from 6 percent as imports continue to rise sharply. Vehicles assembled within the EU will not be covered, while EU-made cars produced in China will be. China also agreed to reduce certain tariffs on European goods, as Brussels shifts toward restraining imports amid concern over its growing trade deficit with Beijing.
stories.headline: EU to cap Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports at 350,000 a year

stories.body: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died and 84 others were missing after an overcrowded boat sank while traveling from Djibouti to Yemen on the night of October 8-9, according to the International Organization for Migration. Most of those aboard were Ethiopian, and the vessel capsized off the coast north of Obock in Djibouti.
stories.headline: At least 139 migrants die in boat sinking between Djibouti and Yemen

stories.body: India's main opposition Congress party led a march to the Supreme Court demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner amid allegations of vote theft and wider protests over the Electoral Commission. Demonstrators faced detentions that the Supreme Court characterized as illegal, according to French press reporting.
stories.headline: Indian opposition marches on Supreme Court seeking election chief's resignation

stories.body: President Donald Trump is facing criticism from Republicans and Democrats over a planned deal to import Russian diesel as fuel prices rise during the Iran war. Trump said Russia would immediately release 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by further shipments, while the Treasury is understood to be suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7. Seven senators said the plan violated a 2022 ban on Russian energy imports and urged Trump to reverse course, while the administration argued that existing legal authorities could be used to lower prices for consumers.
stories.headline: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over planned Russian diesel imports

stories.body: The Trump-aligned super PAC MAGA Inc. plans to narrow its late-cycle congressional battlefield, withdrawing money from House contests it sees as less attainable while increasing spending in races it believes Republicans can still win. Republican officials identified Senate races in Ohio, Alaska and Iowa as increasingly important to preserving the party's majority, while Texas remains an expensive concern. The group and its affiliates have spent more than $200 million of a war chest exceeding $400 million, as Republican candidates confront voter concerns over Trump's approval ratings, the Iran war, tariffs and high fuel prices.
stories.headline: MAGA Inc. plans late spending shifts to defend Republican majorities

stories.body: The Supreme Court's new term could further define how far the Roberts Court is willing to go in reshaping the boundary between church and state, after a series of decisions that have broadened protections for religious rights in the United States.
stories.headline: Supreme Court term could further expand religious-rights protections

stories.body: Moroccan naval vessels, including at least one frigate and several patrol boats, entered Spanish waters off Ceuta without authorization during the mass arrival of more than 70,000 migrants from Morocco on July 30 and 31, according to reports confirmed by Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Spanish naval forces deployed a frigate to halt the incursions, which reportedly continued into early August and nearly led to a collision. Sánchez said the two countries' navies addressed the incident and emphasized the importance of Spain's broader relationship with Morocco.
stories.headline: Moroccan warships reportedly entered Spanish waters near Ceuta during mass migration

stories.body: Podemos and the Catalan Republican Left party, ERC, formalized a campaign agreement under which Podemos will not contest Catalonia's four constituencies in the November 29 general election and its leader Irene Montero will campaign with ERC's Gabriel Rufián. The arrangement has intensified tensions among parties seeking a broader alliance to the left of the Socialist Party. The Comuns accused Rufián of deepening divisions, while negotiations over a unified Frente Amplio ticket, its candidate and Podemos's possible participation remain unresolved days before the coalition-registration deadline.
stories.headline: ERC and Podemos agreement adds to divisions on Spain's left

stories.body: The USS John Basilone is due to arrive at the naval base in Rota, Cádiz, on Thursday, becoming the sixth US guided-missile destroyer deployed there. Its arrival completes an expansion agreed by Spain's Pedro Sánchez and then-US President Joe Biden at the 2022 NATO summit in Madrid, strengthening the US naval presence in Spain even as Washington reduces troops elsewhere in Europe.
stories.headline: Sixth US guided-missile destroyer set to arrive at Rota base

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court has approved a ruling that challenges the Supreme Court's interpretation of the amnesty law and directs it to apply the measure to the alleged misuse of public funds connected to Catalonia's independence process. The decision establishes constitutional doctrine on the law and could allow former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont to return to Spain nine years after leaving the country following the independence crisis.
stories.headline: Amnesty ruling could clear path for Carles Puigdemont's return to Spain

stories.body: Barcelona's October 12 holiday was shaped by the continuing housing protest encampment in Plaça de Catalunya and by competing demonstrations ahead of the general election. Unionist organizations marched on Passeig de Gràcia under the slogan “Catalonia with Ceuta. One Spain,” while anti-fascist and anti-racist groups organized separate protests against the holiday and Spain's colonial past. Housing encampments in Barcelona, Madrid and other cities have kept the affordability crisis at the center of the election campaign after the death of an elderly woman who was evicted in Madrid.
stories.headline: Housing encampment and opposing demonstrations mark October 12 in Barcelona

stories.body: The Mossos d'Esquadra are investigating the violent death of a man after he was attacked by a group of people, possibly with a knife, early Monday in the Roquetes neighborhood of Barcelona's Nou Barris district. Police received the alert at about 2 a.m. on Carrer de Romaní, where officers and emergency crews tried to revive the victim before he died. Barcelona's Criminal Investigation Division has opened an inquiry, which is under judicial secrecy.
stories.headline: Mossos investigate fatal group stabbing in Nou Barris

stories.body: Barcelona's TMB bus workers have called partial strikes on seven days in October, with stoppages remaining on October 14, 15, 20, 22, 27 and 29 after an initial action on October 8. Workers are demanding a reduction from roughly 37.5 to 35 hours per week and two consecutive days off, a rest-day entitlement unions say has been backed by the courts but not implemented. Service disruptions will affect the morning and evening, as well as late-night operations, with minimum service levels set between 20 and 40 percent.
stories.headline: TMB bus workers schedule seven October strike days over hours and rest days
